column12: Judgement on the comparator, house convention: a per-beneficiary spend, not an annual list price, and never annualised. Part B carries the product; the Part D companion (4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15) holds 476 Tecentriq beneficiaries for 2025. Alternative from the same Part B file, 2025: Imfinzi, the other first-line ES-SCLC PD-L1, $60,156.97 (18,812 beneficiaries). The case for higher: BMS-986489 is two antibodies in one vial, and Bristol's other nivolumab FDC, Opdualag, reads $156,530.68 (2,911) against Opdivo and Opdivo Qvantig together at $72,867.59 (28,186), 2.15x. Pricing BMS-986489 like Opdualag would roughly double this value. The case for lower: first-line ES-SCLC patients stay on therapy for about six months (the asset's own Phase 2 BICR PFS of 5.78 months), so an SCLC beneficiary's spend is well under a year of therapy, while Tecentriq's figure mixes in longer adjuvant NSCLC and HCC courses. The first draft used Tecentriq's 2024 annual file, $66,497

column12: Treat-to-progression, so the PFS route, on the asset's own data as the Ris-Rez and ABBV-706 seeds use theirs. The first draft took the TIGOS control regimen, IMpower133's 5.2 months (Horn et al., N Engl J Med 2018;379:2220-2229, PMID 30280641), which gives 0.798. The case for slower stopping: investigator-assessed PFS in the same Phase 2 was 6.47 months, which gives 0.723. The case for faster: real-world PFS from first-line chemoimmunotherapy is 4.2 months (Le et al., Clin Lung Cancer 2026, Komodo), which gives 0.862. The Phase 2 dosed the two antibodies separately, not as the FDC

column11: BMS FY2025 10-K (0000014272-26-000004), Ono alliance note, read in the book's filing_sections copy: BMS 'has the exclusive right to develop, manufacture and commercialize Opdivo and Opdivo Qvantig worldwide except in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. Ono is entitled to receive royalties of 4% in North America and 15% in all territories excluding the three countries listed above, subject to customary adjustments. Ono also receives royalties on the nivolumab component of Opdualag consistent with the terms previously stated for Opdivo.' BMS-986489 and atigotatug are not named. Bristol's J.P. Morgan deck of 12 January 2026 (8-K 0001140361-26-000929, exhibit) lists its development partnerships as 'Anti-CCR8 + nivolumab, nivolumab + relatlimab HD, OPDIVO, YERVOY: Ono; ...' and carries 'atigotatug + nivolumab, 1L Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer' among its Phase III programmes with no partner named. Bristol is lead sponsor of NCT06646276 and NCT06799286 (book trials table)
column12: JUDGEMENT, and a ceiling. No filing names a partner, a royalty or a royalty base for BMS-986489, so the share is 1.0 under the brief's rule (from a filing, else 1.0) and the book's practice for an undisclosed royalty (ABBV-706, GSK5784283: not charged, and said so). The case against: the FDC contains nivolumab, and Bristol pays Ono 4% in North America and 15% in other territories outside Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Opdivo, Opdivo Qvantig and the nivolumab component of Opdualag. A royalty on the nivolumab component of this FDC is therefore likely, but how that component is valued is not disclosed even for Opdualag, and neither is the royalty term. Bounds on BMY's cost rows (margin 1 - 0.2892 cogs - 0.1508 SG&A - 0.2065 R&D - 0 other = 0.3535, lookup.py seed Mavacamten) and the 0.7021 ex-US weight: the blended rate is (4% x 1.0 + 15% x 0.7021) / 1.7021 = 8.537% of revenue, so the share is 0.7585 if the royalty fell on all of the FDC's sales. The first draft's 0.8787 set the component at 0.5023 of sales, Opdivo's over Opdualag's 2024 Part B spend per beneficiary ($71,752 / $142,849). That is a spend ratio across different indications and durations, not a disclosed royalty base, so it is not used. In Japan, South Korea and Taiwan the Ono alliance shares profits equally on combinations of both parties' compounds; those markets sit outside the exus_multiple and are not modelled. The Merck patent agreement is income, not a cost: Merck pays BMS and Ono 2.5% of Keytruda sales through 2026, shared 75/25 (10-Q 0000014272-26-000020). Checked 2026-09-26 in the 10-K itself: its pipeline chart lists 'atigotatug + nivolumab, 1L ES-SCLC' without the mark whose footnote reads 'Development Partnerships: Anti-CCR8 + nivolumab, nivolumab + relatlimab HD, OPDIVO, YERVOY: Ono', so Bristol does not report it as an Ono partnership. The lowest filed tier, 4% in North America, is a low-single-digit royalty the book quotes rather than nets

column11: Three filters. (1) SCLC was 11.8% of new US lung cancers in 2019, and (2) 70.9% of SCLC was extensive-stage at diagnosis over 2000-2019 (Wells et al., JTO Clin Res Rep 2025;6(4):100799, doi:10.1016/j.jtocrr.2025.100799, PMID 40104389, SEER 17). These are the book's own two filters from the ABBV-706 seed, reused. (3) 43.4% of newly diagnosed ES-SCLC patients received antineoplastic therapy: 6,838 of 15,763 in SEER-Medicare, 2001-2013 (Shah et al., JCO Oncol Pract 2020;16(7):e610-e621, doi:10.1200/JOP.19.00559, PMID 32074011). 0.118 x 0.709 x 0.4338 = 0.036293, about 8,226 first-line patients a year on the book's 226,650
column12: Judgement on filter (3). The label is first-line ES-SCLC with carboplatin and etoposide. TIGOS selects on no biomarker (fucosyl-GM1 is expressed on up to 90% of SCLC cells), so only line and stage filter. The case for keeping it: a population-based Canadian cohort agrees, 903 of 1,941 ES-SCLC patients (46.5%) initiating first-line chemotherapy in Alberta, 2010-2018 (O'Sullivan et al., Curr Oncol 2021, PMC8395392, opened 2026-09-26). The case for higher: the 43.4% is Medicare patients aged 65 and over from 2001-2013 and was falling to 36.6% by 2013; younger patients are treated more often, and in Flatiron's oncology-clinic population 8,191 of 9,952 SCLC patients (82%) received at least one line (Shaw et al., Oncologist 2024, PMC11630770), though patients who never see an oncologist are missing from that base. Book inconsistency to flag, not fixed here: the ABBV-706 and Ris-Rez seeds apply Sankar's later-line shares to all ES-SCLC rather than to treated ES-SCLC, so Ris-Rez's second-line pool (0.0323, 7,319 a year) is nearly as large as this first-line pool (8,226 a year)

column11: Incumbent capture: EP plus anti-PD-L1 (atezolizumab or durvalumab) went from 7% of US first-line ES-SCLC regimens in 2018 to 68% in 2019 and about 80% by 2021 (Shaw et al., Oncologist 2024;29(12):1079-1089, doi:10.1093/oncolo/oyae234, PMID 39349396, Flatiron, 4,593 patients). Atezolizumab-based regimens were 89.5% of 2,788 first-line chemoimmunotherapy patients and durvalumab-based 10.5% (Le et al., Clin Lung Cancer 2026;27(4):41-46.e3, PMID 41904053, Komodo claims 2018-2023). Tecentriq therefore holds about 0.80 x 0.895 = 0.716 of first-line regimens
column12: JUDGEMENT: the multiple is 0.5x Tecentriq's measured capture, so 0.5 x 0.716 = 0.358, about 2,945 US patients a year at peak. The measure matches the engine's basis: with prevalence equal to incidence, the peak is the share of each year's first-line patients started on the drug. Bounds: durvalumab, a second PD-L1 with no head-to-head edge, took 10.5% of chemoimmunotherapy patients (Le et al. 2026), 0.117x Tecentriq's share, and a TIGOS OS win against atezolizumab would make BMS-986489 the regimen to replace, up to 1.0x. The case for higher: chemo-PD-L1 displaced EP from 7% to 68% of first-line regimens in a single year after IMpower133 (Shaw et al. 2024). The case for lower: the randomised Phase 2 posted OS of 16.26 against 13.08 months over nivolumab plus chemotherapy, HR 0.80 with a 95% CI of 0.54 to 1.18 that crosses 1 (NCT04702880 results, ClinicalTrials.gov, 2026-06-17). By 2030 first line will be contested by Bristol's own pumitamig (BNT327, a 50/50 profit share with BioNTech, so the two partly cannibalise one another), Pfizer's PF-08634404 (NCT07226999), and tarlatamab and lurbinectedin moving into first-line maintenance

The case for steeper: in this same setting, chemo-PD-L1 went from 7% to 68% of first-line regimens in its first year (Shaw et al. 2024). A logistic fitted to those points would have k near 4, because every first-line patient is new each year and there is no stock to convert. The Enhertu fit is kept because that step rode a first-in-class OS benefit over chemotherapy alone with no IO rival, where BMS-986489 has to displace an entrenched PD-L1 against several newer entrants
